newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway gas body backs developed fields for supply.
newsitem.headline: Norway gas body backs developed fields for supply.

text.p: Norway's Gas Supply Committee (FU) has recommended to the Energy Ministry that spare capacity at the Troll, Oseberg and Sleipner areas in the North Sea should be used to cover gas deliveries to continental Europe from 1998 to 2000, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil ) said on Friday.
A majority of the oil companies in the 12-membered FU also recommended that gas production from Gullfaks satellites should begin in 1999, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
In addition, the FU recommended that the Heidrun and Norne fields in the Norwegian Sea be ensured contracts for associated gas produced at the developments from 2000.

Statoil said 520 billion cubic metres of gas deliveries to Europe had still to be divided up between fields on the Norwegian continental shelf. The FU's latest recommendations covers around 12 percent, or 60 billion cubic metres, of the outstanding gas volumes.
Another allocation round could occur next year, Statoil said.

"The remaining, unallocated volumes prepare the ground for phasing in new field sources from 2001, and gives the necessary time to modify field development concepts for a range of gas prospects in the portfolio," the FU said in a letter to the Energy Ministry.
Eleven fields were considered by the FU in this round of allocations, Statoil said. The Energy Ministry is expected to announce its recommendations by the end of the year.
